beats: A ruler once came home from a trip, pulled out a razor at his own welcome party, and started shaving his guests!
In 1698, the tsar returned from Western Europe, where the fashionable men were clean-shaven.
His name was Peter the Great, and at six foot eight, nobody argued.
One by one, Russia's proudest nobles lost their beards to his own hand.
To many Russians, a beard was holy, and shaving it was a sin.
Soon, police could shave any bearded man on sight!
Then Peter offered a deal: keep your beard, but pay for it every year.
A rich merchant paid up to a hundred rubles.
A peasant paid a kopek every time he walked through the city gates.
Payers had to carry a copper token stamped with a nose, a mouth and a beard!
One version even carried a message: the beard is a superfluous burden.
But some shaved men had a bigger worry.
An English captain met a carpenter who kept his cut-off beard tucked inside his coat.
He planned to be buried with it, so he could explain himself to Saint Nicholas!
The tax outlived Peter by almost fifty years.
All because one tsar came home and reached for a razor!
